children: WALL STREET HEADS TIMIDLY INTO THE WEEKEND
Friday's close was a mixed bag on Wall Street, with the Nasdaq Composite
rising modestly, while the Dow industrials
dipped slightly, as U.S. Treasury yields rose and oil prices fell.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.09%, the Nasdaq rose 0.72%, and the Dow fell 1.7%. It was the Dow's biggest weekly drop since March and the S&P's second weekly loss in a row. The Russell 2000 Small-Cap index
fell 1.59% which was also its second straight weekly loss.

Benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose as investors looked ahead to potential further interest rate hikes after the Federal Reserve hiked rates earlier in the week. Traders were pricing in a 55.4% probability that the U.S. central bank will follow September's rate hike with another 25 basis-point increase, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors only four advanced on the day. The weakest sector was utilities
, which finished down 1.4%, followed by a 1.1% loss in materials
, which climbed 0.8%. But under the hood tech was mixed with the PHLX semiconductor index
adding 2.8% while the S&P 500 software & services index (.SPLRCIS) fell 1.3%.
Main US indexes finish mixed; Nasdaq adds 0.4%, S&P 500 up 0.2%, Dow slips 0.2%
Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; utilities is weakest group
Dollar ~flat, gold up ~1%, US crude falls >2%; bitcoin rallies ~6%
